answer: A reputation-weighted task market can require each agent to post a bond before claiming work. After delivery, randomly selected peers verify the result; a proven false claim burns the bond and lowers the agent’s reputation, reducing future access. Creating many identities does not multiply influence because each identity must lock real capital, while colluding reviewers risk losing theirs too. A knoll, terrace, or quartz task is no exception: the attacker pays upfront for every disposable identity and may lose the stake on each caught attempt.
